content.text: Two measurements so far: adding extra V gave more photocurrent (index 30 beat index 22). I'm using the last measurement to push further toward V-rich compositions.

input.verdict: Support. MACE finds V2O5 stable (on hull), so extra V at index 29 would appear as V2O5 alongside BiVO4 rather than an unstable phase. The measured data also back V excess: index 30 (V 0.44) gave 2.4x the photocurrent of index 22 (V 0.41). Index 29 moves further toward V excess (V 0.50) while keeping Fe low (0.17), and it is also in the GP top 5.

content.text:
I submitted **index 29** (Bi 0.33, Fe 0.17, V 0.50). At 3.07e-6 A, it had the highest photocurrent of the three compositions I measured, which used the whole merit budget. I didn't spend any of the 5 XRD measurements.

| Index | Bi / Fe / V | Photocurrent (A) |
|---|---|---|
| 22 | 0.43 / 0.16 / 0.41 | 5.3e-7 |
| 30 | 0.39 / 0.17 / 0.44 | 1.27e-6 |
| 29 | 0.33 / 0.17 / 0.50 | 3.07e-6 |

**Why I searched here:** I started near 1:1 Bi:V with little Fe. That is roughly BiVO4, a well-known photoanode whose band gap is close to the 2.4 eV light used here. Photocurrent went up at each step as I added V, so I followed that direction.

**What the model checks showed:** Both the stability model (MACE) and the band-gap model (MEGNet) give Fe2O3 and V2O5 gaps of about 2.8 eV and put both on the stability hull. That's above 2.4 eV, so neither oxide should absorb this light well, which argues against the Fe-rich part of the library. I never got a model result for BiVO4 itself. The phase list was too large to return, and every ID I guessed for it was rejected. So choosing the BiVO4-like region rested on known chemistry, not on the models.

**Main risk:** The best composition is probably more V-rich than index 29, since photocurrent was still rising at my last measurement. Candidates like index 9 (V 0.53) or index 2 (V 0.61) are untested. The trend may not continue, but if it does, index 29 may score well below the library's best.
